evidence: Reproduction: (1) A whole-seat leave L removes seat-wide intent and publishes a seat-system-channel instruction for other clones to leave individually; completion may lag and unavailable clones keep pending work (DESIGN-NOTES.md:57; CURRENT-DESIGN.md:40). (2) A newer whole-seat join J commits before clone B handles L; seat-wide intent is inherited by clones, and actual membership may temporarily differ from graph intent (DESIGN-NOTES.md:13-14; CURRENT-DESIGN.md:38). (3) B subsequently handles L as an individual leave; that operation records a clone-specific opt-out, so load does not immediately undo it (DESIGN-NOTES.md:13). No recipient-side instruction revision/current-intent check is specified in the whole-seat leave contract (DESIGN-NOTES.md:57; CURRENT-DESIGN.md:40); the external-action check in latest-intent reconciliation applies to graph-driven effects, not to a later agent submission of an old instruction (DESIGN-NOTES.md:179). (4) B can therefore remain outside the thread despite J being the newer committed whole-seat intent, contrary to the explicit requirement to follow latest committed intent and reconcile performed effects toward it (CURRENT-DESIGN.md:16; DESIGN-NOTES.md:179; HERDR-GRAPH-VISION.md:98). This is an acknowledged open detail only in the different sense of how a later join treats genuine preexisting opt-outs (DESIGN-NOTES.md:13). The finding establishes a design gap, not observed implementation data loss.
